newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso closes weaker, but off early lows.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso closes weaker, but off early lows.

text.p: Mexico's peso pared their early losses, but still closed with a hefty decline on Tuesday as high U.S. interest rates and political worries hurt the currency.
"The market was very unstable, but we were helped by foreign investors who stopped demanding dollars when U.S. long bond rates fell back down," a trader said.
Peso 24-hour and 48-hour contracts closed 3.4 and 3.25 centavos weaker at 7.57/7.5750 and 7.5730/7.5775 per dollar, respectively, after hitting lows of 7.5975/7.6025 and 7.60/7.6050 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bond rates had fallen to 7.07 percent, compared to 7.17 percent in early trade.

Traders said that expectations that local interest rates would gain between 100 and 200 basis points at Tuesday's primary auction also helped to stem the flow of dollars out of Mexico and prevent the peso from weakening further.
"Volatility in the U.S. debt market makes an upward adjustment necessary in Mexican Cetes rates," a currency trader said.
The same-day peso previously closed 0.7 centavos weaker at 7.57/7.5740 per dollar.

The peso may have also been hurt by mounting political worries for the government. Earlier, Zapatista rebels suspended peace talks with the government, which is also trying to put out a new guerrilla movement in southern Mexico.

In a signal that Mexican officials do not mind seeing a slightly weaker peso, Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said the government is wary of the peso becoming overvalued and would not use it as an anchor for inflation.
